dedupe_keys.name: frame flood resilience agent based model community flood resilience with governance networks in a mekong river basin settlement

description: FRAMe is an agent-based framework that simulates flood resilience at community level in a rural settlement of the Mekong River Basin. The CoMSES Net release read on 2026-09-28 (version 1.0.0, published 22 October 2025 by Wenhan Feng, modified 3 January 2026) combines empirical data from extensive surveys, Bayesian networks and hydrological simulations, and measures resilience as a trade-off between robustness, meaning resistance to damage, and adaptability, meaning the capacity to respond. Households, governments and other actors are linked by social and governance networks that carry knowledge, resources and risk messages, and the model includes flood forecasting and policy interventions such as education, aid and insurance, with decisions grounded in Protection Motivation Theory and the MoHuB framework. It is spatially explicit with GIS inputs and is written in NetLogo with R. Coverage is one rural settlement in the Mekong basin. Access is free download under the Academic Free Licence 3.0. Caveats: the settlement is not named in the summary, and the survey data may not be bundled. It supports resilience and adaptation studies, such as comparing aid and insurance policies for flood-prone villages. No related Mekong flood resilience model is catalogued.
name: FRAMe (Flood Resilience Agent-Based Model): community flood resilience with governance networks in a Mekong River Basin settlement
outputs: robustness and adaptability of households and community
effects of education, aid and insurance policies
